title_en: Zhang Yufang v. Xie Yumin, Shenzhen Aoxinlong Investment Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over other contract
ruling_gist_en: Transfer for security (rang yu dan bao), as a security measure, constitutes an accessory contract. It can only arise when a principal contract exists. Therefore, whether a principal contract exists and a transfer for security is established based on it is an important prerequisite and criterion for judging whether a relevant transaction arrangement constitutes a transfer for security. The agreement between the parties in an ordinary transfer contract that the transferor may repurchase the transferred property within a certain period is a commercial arrangement agreed upon by the parties, which is different from the agreement in a transfer for security that the transferor shall repurchase the transferred property after the expiration of a certain period. When determining whether a transaction arrangement concerning equity is a transfer for security or an equity transfer, factors such as whether the transferee's shareholder rights are restricted and whether the transferee has enjoyed complete shareholder rights should be considered comprehensively.

full_text_en:
Zhang Yufang v. Xie Yumin, Shenzhen Ao Xinlong Investment Co., Ltd. et al.

— Dispute over Other Contract

Ruling Summary

Suretyship by transfer of title, as a type of security measure, constitutes an ancillary contract. Only when a principal contract exists can a suretyship by transfer arise. Therefore, whether a principal contract exists and serves as the basis for establishing a suretyship by transfer is an important prerequisite and standard for determining whether the relevant transaction arrangement constitutes a suretyship by transfer. The agreement in an ordinary transfer contract that the transferor may repurchase the transferred property within a certain period is a commercial arrangement agreed upon by the parties, which differs from the agreement in a suretyship by transfer that the transferor shall repurchase the transferred property after the expiration of a certain period. In determining whether a transaction arrangement concerning equity is a suretyship by transfer or an equity transfer, factors such as whether the transferee's shareholder rights are restricted and whether the transferee has already enjoyed complete shareholder rights shall be comprehensively considered.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2020) Zui Gao Fa Shang Chu No. 5

Plaintiff: Zhang Yufang (ZHANG YUFANG) (former Chinese name: Zhang Yufang), male, born on September 25, 1956, citizen of Belize.

Agent ad litem: Li Zhao, lawyer of Beijing Global Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Chengjie, lawyer of Beijing Global Law Firm Shanghai Office.

Defendant: Xie Yumin, male, born on May 17, 1989, Han ethnicity, residing at Dongcheng District, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Ji Buynnasen, lawyer of Beijing Deheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Yi, lawyer of Beijing JunZeJun (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Defendant: Shenzhen Ao Xinlong Investment Co., Ltd. Address: Units A, E, and F, 41/F, Huangting Building, No. 3038 Jintian Road, Futian Street, Futian District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Yao Jianhong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Yu, lawyer of Beijing JunZeJun (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Defendant: Liu Hechao, male, born on October 3, 1953, resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, currently residing at Dongguan City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Zhifan, lawyer of Beijing Guantao Zhongmao (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

Defendant: Chen Jing, male, born on June 6, 1962, Han ethnicity, residing at Futian District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province, People's Republic of China.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hong, lawyer of Tahota (Shenzhen) Law Firm.

With respect to the case of dispute over other contract between the plaintiff Zhang Yufang and the defendants Xie Yumin, Shenzhen Ao Xinlong Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ao Xinlong Company), Liu Hechao, and Chen Jing, the Intermediate People's Court of Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Intermediate Court) accepted the case on July 3, 2019. Pursuant to Article 38, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2017) and Article 2, Item 5 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Establishment of International Commercial Courts, this Court rendered the (2020) Zui Gao Fa Min Xia No. 54 Civil Ruling on September 29, 2020, ruling that this case shall be tried by the First International Commercial Court of this Court. After this case was filed on December 17, 2020, this Court held a public hearing on December 10, 2021. Li Zhao and Wang Chengjie, agents ad litem of the plaintiff Zhang Yufang; Ji Buynnasen and Cheng Yi, agents ad litem of the defendant Xie Yumin; Zhao Yu, agent ad litem of the defendant Ao Xinlong Company; Zheng Zhifan, agent ad litem of the defendant Liu Hechao; and Jiang Hong, agent ad litem of the defendant Chen Jing appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Zhang Yufang submitted the following claims to the Shenzhen Intermediate Court: 1. To confirm that the 99% equity interest in Shenzhen Meidafei Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Meidafei Company) registered in the name of Ao Xinlong Company is a suretyship by transfer of equity provided by Zhang Yufang to Xie Yumin and Ao Xinlong Company, and that a suretyship by transfer relationship has been formed; 2. To confirm that the 99% equity interest in Meidafei Company registered in the name of the defendant Ao Xinlong Company belongs to Zhang Yufang; 3. To confirm that Xie Yumin, Ao Xinlong Company, Liu Hechao, and Chen Jing are jointly and severally liable for compensating Zhang Yufang for the loss of RMB 500,000 (hereinafter all amounts are in RMB) caused by their breach of the "Equity Repurchase Agreement," "Letter of Undertaking," and "Settlement Agreement"; 4. To order Xie Yumin, Ao Xinlong Company, Liu Hechao, and Chen Jing to bear the litigation costs and preservation fees of this case.

At the pre-trial conference held on December 6, 2021, Zhang Yufang applied to amend his claims as follows: 1. To confirm that a suretyship by transfer legal relationship exists among Zhang Yufang, Anshan Dafei Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dafei Company), and Xie Yumin, and that the 99% equity interest in Meidafei Company registered in the name of Ao Xinlong Company is a suretyship by transfer of equity provided by Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company to Xie Yumin; 2. To confirm that the 43.86% equity interest in Meidafei Company registered in the name of Ao Xinlong Company belongs to Zhang Yufang; 3. To order Xie Yumin, Ao Xinlong Company, Liu Hechao, and Chen Jing to be jointly and severally liable for compensating Zhang Yufang for the loss of RMB 500,000; 4. To order Xie Yumin, Ao Xinlong Company, Liu Hechao, and Chen Jing to bear the litigation costs, preservation fees, and guarantee fees of this case.

Facts and reasons: (I) In order to repay the RMB 619 million loan borrowed from Chen Jing et al. for the development of the Shenzhen Dali Garden Project and the Meidafei Fuyong Project, Zhang Yufang and the relevant entities under his control (the "Dafei Group") transferred 100% of the equity in Meidafei Company as a suretyship by transfer to Shenzhen Chuangdongfang Xingdi Investment Enterprise (Limited Partnership) (hereinafter referred to as Chuangdongfang Enterprise) to obtain financing of RMB 610 million from Chuangdongfang Enterprise. To repay the debt to Chuangdongfang Enterprise, Zhang Yufang and Liu Hechao signed a "Confirmation Letter" on November 24, 2014, and a "Principle Framework Agreement on the Repayment of Financing from Chuangdongfang by Dafei Technology Company and Ao Xinlong Company, Shareholders of Meidafei Company" (hereinafter referred to as the "Principle Framework Agreement") on December 22, 2014. These agreements stipulated that Liu Hechao would repay the debt owed by the Dafei Group to Chuangdongfang Enterprise on its behalf, and Zhang Yufang would provide a suretyship by transfer through the Meidafei equity and guarantee to repay Liu Hechao's loan within 12 months through a premium-based equity purchase. (II) On December 19 and 22, 2014, after Liu Hechao repaid RMB 682.555 million on behalf of the Dafei Group to Chuangdongfang Enterprise, he designated Xie Yumin as the creditor for the RMB 682.555 million and together with Zhang Yufang and other Dafei Group entities, signed the "Equity Repurchase Agreement." It stipulated that: (1) The 99% equity in Meidafei Company redeemed from Chuangdongfang Enterprise would be registered in the name of Ao Xinlong Company, as designated by Xie Yumin, as a suretyship by transfer for the RMB 682.555 million loan; (2) Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company would repurchase the 99% equity in Meidafei Company at a premium of RMB 1.1 billion within 12 months, and Xie Yumin's side guaranteed that they would not demand early repurchase during the repurchase period; (3) If the proceeds from disposing of the 99% equity in Meidafei Company were insufficient to repay Xie Yumin's side, Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company would be liable for the shortfall; any excess would belong to Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company; (4) During the period when Xie Yumin's side held the equity in Meidafei Company, if China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., Shenzhen Branch (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Company) were to invest in the Meidafei project, both parties should cooperate to facilitate the transaction. If the transaction price could not cover the debt, Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company must provide other effective guarantees; (5) The agreement also provided for other security measures and the obligation of Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company to provide additional security if the collateral value was insufficient. (III) On September 5, 2015, the parties agreed to extend the repurchase period to March 21, 2016, and increased the repurchase price to RMB 1.257 billion accordingly. On September 6, 2015, the Dafei Group and Chuangdongfang Enterprise confirmed the termination of the "Meidafei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement." Chuangdongfang Enterprise released the Meidafei equity, and Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company, in accordance with the "Equity Repurchase Agreement," arranged for the registration of the 99% equity in Meidafei Company in the name of Ao Xinlong Company. After the "Equity Repurchase Agreement" was signed, Zhang Yufang reached a cooperation plan with Cinda Company for the Meidafei Fuyong Project, which was approved by the headquarters of Cinda Company. If this plan had been implemented, Zhang Yufang would have been fully able to repay the debt to Xie Yumin's side within the agreed repurchase period and redeem the Meidafei equity. However, in order to obstruct Zhang Yufang from obtaining financing from Cinda Company to redeem the equity, Xie Yumin and Liu Hechao not only refused to cooperate with due diligence but also colluded with Chen Jing, Zhao Hailong, and Zhao Duangeng to engage in false litigation and maliciously freeze the Meidafei equity. Currently, Zhao Hailong and Zhao Duangeng are under criminal investigation by the Futian Branch of the Shenzhen Public Security Bureau. Due to the malicious obstruction by Xie Yumin and others, Zhang Yufang was unable to redeem the equity within the agreed repurchase period. To protect his legal rights, Dafei Company filed a lawsuit before the repurchase period expired on March 11, 2016, with the Higher People's Court of Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as Guangdong High Court), which became Case No. (2017) Yue Min Chu 1 (hereinafter referred to as Case 1). As that case did not allow Zhang Yufang to join as a co-plaintiff nor did it allow Dafei Company to withdraw the lawsuit, Zhang Yufang separately initiated this case. (IV) Based on the above facts, Zhang Yufang contends that: 1. Liu Hechao and Xie Yumin provided a loan of RMB 682.555 million to Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company, and the 99% equity in Meidafei Company registered in the name of Ao Xinlong Company is a suretyship by transfer of equity provided by Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company to Xie Yumin. (1) The "Confirmation Letter" and the "Principle Framework Agreement" clearly established the loan and suretyship by transfer relationship between Liu Hechao and Zhang Yufang. (2) The "Equity Repurchase Agreement" further clarified the loan and suretyship by transfer relationship between Xie Yumin and Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company. (3) Subsequent actions such as extensions and settlements after the "Equity Repurchase Agreement" all indicate that the relationship between Xie Yumin and Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company is one of loan and suretyship by transfer, not equity transfer. 2. The 43.86% equity in Meidafei Company registered in the name of Ao Xinlong Company belongs to Zhang Yufang. Ao Xinlong Company was originally controlled by Zhang Yufang and held 43.86% equity in Meidafei Company. During the signing of the "Equity Repurchase Agreement," Ao Xinlong Company had no independent will; rather, under the arrangement of its shareholders, its 100% equity was used as a shell vehicle, transferred to Xie Yumin at zero consideration to facilitate Xie Yumin's control over the collateral. Therefore, the 43.86% equity in Meidafei Company originally held by Ao Xinlong Company should always belong to Zhang Yufang. 3. According to the "Equity Repurchase Agreement," Xie Yumin and Ao Xinlong Company are obligated to cooperate in facilitating Cinda Company's investment in the Meidafei Company project. Zhang Yufang has been actively promoting this project, but Xie Yumin, Liu Hechao, Ao Xinlong Company, and Chen Jing, by refusing to cooperate with the project's due diligence and filing false lawsuits, have maliciously obstructed Zhang Yufang from obtaining financing from Cinda Company to repurchase the Meidafei equity. They should be jointly and severally liable for compensating Zhang Yufang for the loss of financing costs, and Zhang Yufang reserves the right to seek compensation for other losses. In summary, the Dafei Group, controlled by Zhang Yufang, initially had external liabilities of RMB 619 million but held two core land assets in Bao'an District, Shenzhen, valued at over RMB 10 billion. To repay the usurious loans from Xie Yumin, Chen Jing, and others, Zhang Yufang has already sold the Dali Garden Project to repay debts. Moreover, if the defendants' claims are followed, the Meidafei project will also be illegally encroached upon, resulting in Zhang Yufang not only losing two projects worth billions of yuan but also owing Xie Yumin an additional illegal historical debt of over RMB 500 million. Such an outcome would be extremely unjust and absurd. Zhang Yufang requests the court to uphold all his claims.

This Court has permitted Zhang Yufang's application to add and amend his claims; as for Zhang Yufang's application to join Dafei Company as a third party without independent claims in this case, it is not permitted.

Xie Yumin argued that all of Zhang Yufang's claims should be dismissed. Reasons: (I) The identity documents submitted by Zhang Yufang when filing the lawsuit do not meet the form requirements of Chinese law, and there are significant issues with the authenticity of the civil complaint. 1. Zhang Yufang did not submit identity documents and authorization documents that comply with the Civil Procedure Law, raising significant doubts about the authenticity of his subject identity. 2. The "Application for Amendment of Claims" submitted by Zhang Yufang's representative bears only the representative's signature, raising significant questions as to whether it represents Zhang Yufang's true intention. (II) This case, filed by Zhang Yufang, and Case 1, filed by Dafei Company in the Guangdong High Court, are based on the same facts, have the same core disputes, and essentially the same claims. Moreover, the core evidence in both cases is the "Equity Repurchase Agreement," constituting duplicative litigation. (III) Zhang Yufang, claiming to be the actual controller of Dafei Company, asserts that the equity in question constitutes a suretyship by transfer and requests confirmation that the equity belongs to him. This lacks a necessary basis for the claim, and he has no right to bring this lawsuit. 1. Zhang Yufang is neither the transferor nor the transferee of the equity in question and has no direct legal interest in the disputed equity; 2. The interview record of Case No. (2018) Yue 03 Po Shen 296 from the Shenzhen Intermediate Court shows that Zhang Tao, the major shareholder of Dafei Company, explicitly stated that Zhang Yufang is not the actual controller of Dafei Company and has no indirect interest in this case, thus having no basis for rights and no interest in the litigation; 3. According to the transaction arrangement in the "Equity Repurchase Agreement," at the time the agreement was signed, Ao Xinlong Company had already emerged as a company actually held by Xie Yumin, independent and no longer having any relationship with Zhang Yufang. (IV) The "Equity Repurchase Agreement" is the contractual basis for the equity transfer in question. Through an analysis of the terms of the "Equity Repurchase Agreement," the background, purpose, and method of the equity transaction can be truly reflected, thereby determining that the legal nature of the "Equity Repurchase Agreement" is an equity transfer, not a suretyship by transfer. 1. The purpose of Xie Yumin signing the "Equity Repurchase Agreement" and paying RMB 682.555 million was to acquire the equity in Meidafei Company; 2. The "Equity Repurchase Agreement" contains nine articles, of which the core provisions are Articles 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7. Articles 1, 2, and 3 explicitly stipulate the transaction model, payment amount, payment time, and payment method for this equity transaction, confirming that Ao Xinlong Company is actually held by Xie Yumin. Article 5 entirely pertains to arrangements for the exercise of the repurchase right. Article 6 contains typical representations and warranties of the transferor in an equity transaction, stipulating the transferor's representations and warranties regarding the status of the transferred subject matter. Article 7 provides safeguards for the performance of the "Equity Repurchase Agreement" and the completion of the acquisition of the equity in question; 3. A suretyship by transfer is an act that takes the form of a property transfer with the purpose of securing a principal claim. The RMB 682.555 million paid by Xie Yumin was the consideration for acquiring the equity in Meidafei Company, and no loan fact was created between Xie Yumin and Zhang Yufang. Without a principal claim, how can there be a suretyship by transfer? In addition, at the time the agreement was signed, Zhang Yufang already owed Xie Yumin a huge debt of RMB 548.96 million. Before such debt was repaid, it was impossible for Xie Yumin to provide him with any new loan. 4. After Ao Xinlong Company became a shareholder of Meidafei Company, it actually managed Meidafei Company, including changing its registered address and its directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel, and completing the industrial and commercial registration changes. According to the opinion in the "Meeting Minutes of Judges of the Second Civil Trial Division of the Supreme People's Court," where an investor's purpose is to obtain the target company's equity and the investor enjoys the right to participate in the company's operation and management, it shall be deemed an equity investment, and the investor is a shareholder of the target company. (V) Zhang Yufang's claim that Xie Yumin maliciously obstructed his exercise of the equity purchase right is completely unfounded. 1. Zhang Yufang alleged that Xie Yumin colluded with Chen Jing, Zhao Duangeng, and others to engage in false litigation, but the case (2015) Shen Zhong Fa She Wai Chu No. 274 was a dispute among Zhang Yufang, Dafei Company, Chen Jing, and Zhao Duangeng, and had nothing to do with Xie Yumin; 2. The "Letter of Undertaking" issued to Zhang Yufang by Ao Xinlong Company and Xie Yumin on September 5, 2015, did not obtain an extension because the seven preconditions set forth therein were not met during actual performance. Apart from that, Xie Yumin actively cooperated with Zhang Yufang's applications for seals required for Cinda's due diligence, and there was no malicious obstruction whatsoever.

Ao Xinlong Company argued that all of Zhang Yufang's claims should be dismissed. Reasons: (I) Zhang Yufang does not have the right basis or interest in litigation to bring the claims in this case. 1. Zhang Yufang is not the transferor of the equity in question nor a shareholder of Meidafei Company and has no right to dispute the nature of the equity in question; 2. Whether Zhang Yufang is the actual controller of Meidafei Company remains to be ascertained, and a company legal person has independence; an actual controller who is not a shareholder of the company cannot obtain or dispose of the target company's equity; 3. Whether this case was actually initiated by Zhang Yufang and whether the relevant subject and authorization procedures are lawful still need to be verified. (II) The legal nature of the relationship in question is that of an equity transfer, not a suretyship by transfer. 1. The core provisions of the "Equity Repurchase Agreement" clarify its nature as an equity transfer. Pursuant to Article 125 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, when interpreting the terms of the agreement in question, consideration should be given to literal interpretation, systematic interpretation, and teleological interpretation. It can be found that the agreement is completely different from the characteristics of a suretyship by transfer. After the expiration of the repurchase period, the investor has actually enjoyed shareholder rights. Although the agreement contains terms such as a time-limited purchase right, valuation adjustment, and risk protection, these terms are arrangements made by the parties in the context of an equity transfer and equity investment. They do not change—indeed, they confirm—the nature of the equity transfer in question; 2. In this case, the transferee not only clearly had the intention to become a shareholder and to manage the company but also actually managed Meidafei Company. After the equity transfer in question, Meidafei Company's registered address and its directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel were replaced, and the industrial and commercial registration procedures were completed. In addition, the new shareholder and subsequent investors have done significant work to promote the development of Meidafei Company's land project and to avoid the risk of it being reclaimed by the government; 3. In terms of trade practices, the provisions of the "Equity Repurchase Agreement" in question are completely inconsistent with the customary expressions of Zhang Yufang and the Dafei Group companies in previous cases of suretyship by transfer of equity. They typically used expressions such as "equity holding on behalf of" and explicitly stipulated the return of equity. However, such expressions never appeared in the "Equity Repurchase Agreement"; 4. In terms of good faith, at the time Xie Yumin's side acquired the equity in question, the Meidafei Company land project faced the significant risk of being reclaimed by the government. Both parties were professional businessmen, and their actions were all commercial arrangements and voluntary risk-taking, which were fair and reasonable. (III) Zhang Yufang's claim that Xie Yumin and Ao Xinlong Company obstructed his purchase of the equity in question is completely unfounded. 1. The reply letter issued by Cinda Company, as presented by Zhang Yufang, has no proof of delivery, its true intent is unclear, and there is no objective evidence to corroborate it; 2. Zhang Yufang fails to provide any evidence showing that he claimed the equity repurchase within the repurchase period stipulated in the agreement or that Ao Xinlong Company allegedly failed to cooperate with his repurchase. (IV) This case is a frivolous lawsuit filed by Zhang Yufang that repeats the dispute in Case 1 of the Guangdong High Court. Regarding the dispute over the nature of the equity transfer in question, Dafei Company has already filed a related action for declaratory relief in Case 1. The contractual basis, core facts, and main points of contention in this case are the same as those in Case 1, which essentially constitutes vexatious and abusive litigation.

Liu Hechao argued that Zhang Yufang's claims should be dismissed. Reasons: (1) Liu Hechao did not participate in the cooperation between Xie Yumin and Zhang Yufang based on the Share Repurchase Agreement, and Zhang Yufang's allegation that Liu Hechao was the actual controller of Xie Yumin was completely unfounded. The Pre-Framework Agreement for Equity Acquisition and the Principle Framework Agreement signed with Liu Hechao's involvement did not take effect and were not actually performed. (2) Liu Hechao did not participate in signing the Share Repurchase Agreement, the Letter of Undertaking, or the Settlement Agreement and was not a party to them. Zhang Yufang's request for Liu Hechao to bear joint and several compensation of RMB 500,000 for breach of the provisions of such documents obviously lacked factual and legal basis. (3) Zhang Yufang strongly opposed the Supreme People's Court's retrial of this case, which fully demonstrated his abuse of litigation rights.

Chen Jing argued that Zhang Yufang's claims should be dismissed. Reasons: (1) Chen Jing had previously signed a Cooperation Agreement and related supplemental agreements with Zhang Yufang, stipulating that Chen Jing would contribute capital to cooperate with Zhang Yufang and Dafei-related companies on projects, but these were unrelated to the Share Repurchase Agreement. (2) Chen Jing was not a party or signatory to the Share Repurchase Agreement, the Letter of Undertaking, or the Settlement Agreement, and did not receive any benefits from them; therefore, he was not a proper defendant. Zhang Yufang's claim against Chen Jing for joint and several compensation ignored the principle of privity of contract and was entirely without factual or legal basis.

The parties submitted evidence in accordance with the law in support of the plaintiff's claims. The Court organized the parties to exchange evidence and conduct cross-examination. The Court confirmed the evidence to which the parties raised no objection and placed it on the case file. For disputed evidence and facts, the Court will make a comprehensive determination in light of the case facts.

Based on the parties' representations and the evidence examined and confirmed, the Court finds the following facts:

(1) Background of the execution of the Share Repurchase Agreement

In 1995, Meidafei Company was established. Before December 30, 2012, the shareholders of Meidafei Company were Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company, holding 56.14% and 43.86% of the shares, respectively. According to a series of prior agreements signed between Dafei Company and Meidafei Company, Zhang Yufang was the original actual controller of Meidafei Company.

On September 26, 2013, Shenzhen Chuangdongfang Investment Co., Ltd. and Beijing Zhongcai Century Technology Co., Ltd. as Party A, CITIC South China (Group) Shenzhen Co., Ltd. as Party B, Shenzhen Photoelectric Industry Holding Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Photoelectric Company) and Chen Jing as Party C, Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company as Party D, Meidafei Company as Party E, and Zhang Yufang as Party F jointly signed the Meidafei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement. The Meidafei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement stated in the "Recitals" section: On December 30, 2012, Party C and its affiliates signed the Cooperation Agreement (hereinafter referred to as the "Photoelectric Cooperation Agreement") and supplemental agreements with Meidafei Company, the shareholders of Meidafei Company, and affiliates, stipulating that Party C would provide a loan of RMB 660 million to Meidafei Company and its affiliates. As a safeguard measure, 100% equity of Aoxinlong Company, which held 43.86% of Meidafei Company's shares, was transferred to Party C and Xie Yumin. After the execution of the Photoelectric Cooperation Agreement, Party C had disbursed RMB 561 million in loans to Meidafei Company as agreed. Party C and Xie Yumin currently held 100% equity in Aoxinlong Company. The main content of the Meidafei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement was: Party A initiated the establishment of Chuangdongfang Enterprise to conduct debt restructuring for Meidafei Company and its affiliates, and to provide financing services for the Meidafei Fuyong Phase I Project.

On November 19, 2013, Chuangdongfang Enterprise, as one of Party A, joined the cooperation and signed the Supplemental Agreement (II) to the Meidafei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement with Parties B, C, D, E, and F. The main content was: Party D (Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company, which then held 56.14% and 43.86% of Meidafei Company shares, respectively) registered 100% equity of Meidafei Company under the name of Chuangdongfang Enterprise. This was, in nature, a risk safeguard measure provided by Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company for Chuangdongfang Enterprise's investment in Meidafei Company, intended to protect the investment risk of Chuangdongfang Enterprise's fund. At the same time, Chuangdongfang Enterprise and Beijing Zhongcai Century Technology Co., Ltd. undertook in a Letter of Undertaking that, during the period (2+1 years) when Chuangdongfang Enterprise held 100% equity in Meidafei Company, they would not transfer or dispose of the equity held in Meidafei Company to external parties before the recovery of returns.

Thereafter, Chuangdongfang Enterprise paid a total of approximately RMB 610 million to Dafei-related entities, and 100% equity of Meidafei Company was transferred to Chuangdongfang Enterprise.

(2) Execution and main content of the Share Repurchase Agreement

On December 18, 2014, Zhang Yufang as Party A and Liu Hechao as Party B jointly signed the Principle Framework Agreement, the main content of which was: Party B would provide funds to repay the RMB 700 million loan from Chuangdongfang Enterprise on behalf of Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company; when Chuangdongfang Enterprise released the equity of Meidafei Company, 99% of the equity would be held by Aoxinlong Company and 1% by Dafei Company; the provision that Party A designated Party B to purchase the equity of Meidafei Company held by Chuangdongfang Enterprise was canceled.

On December 22, 2014, Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company as Party A, Aoxinlong Company as Party B, Xie Yumin as Party C, Zhang Baochen, Zhang Yan, and Shenzhen Yufang Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yufang Company) as Party D, and Dongguan Yichao Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yichao Company) as Party E jointly signed the Share Repurchase Agreement. The Share Repurchase Agreement stated in the "Recitals" section: Zhang Yufang was the actual controller of Meidafei Company and Dafei Company; in 2014, Meidafei Company obtained financing from Chuangdongfang Enterprise, and as a measure to ensure repayment, 100% equity of Meidafei Company was registered under Chuangdongfang Enterprise; Chuangdongfang Enterprise demanded early repayment of the debt; as of December 31, 2014, Party A's historical debt to Party C was RMB 548.96 million; according to the original agreement, 90% equity of Aoxinlong Company was registered under Party C, and 10% equity was registered under Photoelectric Company, as a guarantee for the above debt of Party A to Party C; before the transfer of 100% equity of Meidafei Company to Chuangdongfang Enterprise, Dafei Company held 56.14% equity in Meidafei Company, and Aoxinlong Company held 43.86% equity. Article 1 (Equity attribute of Aoxinlong Company): Zhang Yufang and Party D agreed that, because Party C held 90% equity in Aoxinlong Company and assisted Party B in raising funds to repurchase Meidafei Company's equity from Chuangdongfang Enterprise, the equity in Aoxinlong Company held by Party C and Photoelectric Company would no longer serve as a guarantee for the aforementioned historical debt; 90% equity of Aoxinlong Company would be formally held by Party C, and 10% equity would be formally held by Photoelectric Company. Party D could repurchase the equity of Aoxinlong Company from Party C and Photoelectric Company, with specific conditions to be separately agreed. Article 2 (Equity repurchase clause): 1. Party B would raise funds not exceeding RMB 700 million (including RMB 230 million from the proceeds of Cinda Company) to repurchase 99% equity of Meidafei Company (Party B's funds would be paid through Party E). 2. When Chuangdongfang Enterprise released the equity of Meidafei Company, 99% equity would be held by Aoxinlong Company, and 1% equity would be held by Dafei Company. 3. Within one year from the repurchase of Meidafei Company's equity (including any extension period agreed by Party B), Party B guaranteed that Meidafei Company would not engage in other unrelated business operations, and cooperation matters of Meidafei Company with external parties would be determined by agreement between Party A and Party B. The relevant seals of Party B and Meidafei Company would be jointly managed by both parties. Article 3 (Financing): After the signing of this agreement, Party B must pay the first installment of RMB 653,569,300 in installments through Party E to Chuangdongfang Enterprise's account by December 24, 2014. Article 4 (Proceeds from Cinda Company): Zhang Yufang guaranteed that the payment of RMB 230 million from Cinda Company for the "Dali Huayuan" project would be received in the account designated by Photoelectric Company at Yichao Company within 3 business days after the completion of the equity registration procedures for Dafei Real Estate Development (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dafei Real Estate Company). This RMB 230 million was part of Party A's repayment of historical debt. Article 5 (Equity purchase right): 1. Party A had the right to purchase 99% equity of Meidafei Company from Party B within 12 months after Party B's repurchase of Meidafei Company's equity (starting from the date of full payment of RMB 653,569,300), at the following purchase prices: if purchased within 6 months after the completion of the equity repurchase of Meidafei Company, the purchase price for Meidafei Company's equity would be RMB 1.03 billion; if purchased after 6 months but within 12 months after the completion of the equity repurchase, the purchase price for all equity of Meidafei Company would be RMB 1.1 billion. 2. When the equity purchase payment reached RMB 700 million, Party B must register 40% equity of Meidafei Company under Zhang Yufang or his designated party, so that Zhang Yufang or his designated party would hold 40% equity of Meidafei Company. 3. After Party A repaid the historical debt to Party C, and Party B had received the equity purchase payment of RMB 700 million from Party A, and the land use certificate for 69,500 square meters of commercial land of Meidafei Company had been obtained, Party A's equity purchase period could be extended by 3 months, with the premium for the extension to be separately negotiated. 4. After Party B repurchased Meidafei Company's equity, and before the land use procedures for the 69,500 square meters of commercial and residential land of Meidafei Company were completed (or before Cinda Company or other actual investors invested in the Meidafei project), Party A agreed that all proceeds from the Dali Huayuan transaction, except for the supplementary land premium, would be collected by Party B. If the amount collected by Party B exceeded the historical debt amount, the excess amount would be treated as Party B's debt to Party A and would accrue interest at an annual rate of 20%. However, if at the expiration of the equity purchase period under this agreement (including any extension agreed by Party B), the land use certificate for the 69,500 square meters of commercial and residential land had not been issued, Party B would not bear interest on the above excess funds. ...5. The parties confirmed that if Party B realized investment proceeds through the disposal of Meidafei Company's equity, after the disposal proceeds fully satisfied Party B's due amounts (historical debt + total equity purchase price under Article 5 of this agreement), the remaining balance would belong to Party A; conversely, if the disposal proceeds were insufficient to satisfy Party B's due amounts, Party A would cover the shortfall. Article 6 (Warranties of each party): 1. Party A warranted that as of the signing of this agreement, the land of Meidafei Company was not subject to any mortgage, seizure, attachment, ownership dispute, or any other circumstances affecting the realization of the land's value. 2. As of the date of signing this agreement, except for debts owed to Chuangdongfang Enterprise and possibly to CITIC-related companies, and possibly to Photoelectric Company and Chen Jing, Meidafei Company had no undisclosed guarantees or debts; otherwise, Party A should bear compensation liability. 3. Zhang Yufang guaranteed that within 12 months from the date Party B completed the repurchase of Meidafei Company's equity, he would clear the premises of the 69,500 square meters of commercial and residential land of Meidafei Company, including but not limited to any items existing on the land due to lease, loan, occupation, or similar relationships. If the clearance was not completed on time, Zhang Yufang should pay RMB 30 million in compensation to Party B, payable within 60 days from the expiration of the period specified in this agreement. In case of delay or insufficient payment, liquidated damages would be payable at a daily rate of 1/1000 of the unpaid amount. 4. Party B guaranteed that it would raise sufficient funds as agreed in this agreement and repurchase 99% equity of Meidafei Company, and would not demand early purchase by Party A within one year or any agreed extension period. If it did, Party A had the right to refuse, and Party B must not sell the equity or assets of Meidafei Company to external parties. 5. After Party B repurchased Meidafei Company's equity, if investors such as Cinda Company invested in the Meidafei project for cooperative real estate development, Party A and Party B should cooperate to facilitate the transaction and handle relevant procedures such as equity transfer, equity pledge, and land mortgage. However, if the transaction payments were insufficient to cover the debt, Party A must provide other effective guarantee measures for Party B. Article 7 (Safeguard clause): ...3. If, due to policy reasons, the plot for which the procedures for improvement had been approved by Meidafei Company was classified as industrial land by the government or its land use could not be changed to commercial/residential, Zhang Yufang should, within 6 months, mortgage the assets of Hong Kong Meida International Business Company in Chengdu and Shenyang to Party B as a safeguard measure for Party B's losses not covered elsewhere. Article 9 (Other clauses): 1. All contracts signed between Zhang Yufang and Liu Hechao before the date of signing this agreement were void, and the provisions of this agreement would prevail. ...

(3) Performance of the Share Repurchase Agreement

After the execution of the Share Repurchase Agreement, from November to December 2014, Meidafei Company paid RMB 17,445,000 to Chuangdongfang Enterprise; Dongguan Yuewen Trade Co., Ltd. paid RMB 28,985,700 to Chuangdongfang Enterprise on behalf of Aoxinlong Company; and Yichao Company paid RMB 653,569,300 to Chuangdongfang Enterprise on behalf of Aoxinlong Company, totaling RMB 700 million.

On February 3, 2015, Photoelectric Company and Chen Jing as Party A, Xie Yumin as Party B, Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company as Party C, Zhang Yufang as Party D, and Wen Jianhe as Party E jointly signed a Supplemental Agreement, the main content of which was: Parties A, B, C, and D had signed an Agreement on December 12, 2014, agreeing to irrevocably transfer the claims of the original creditors against Dafei Company in the amount of RMB 548.96 million (calculated as of December 31, 2014) to Xie Yumin; future debt repayments by Dafei Company would be made to Xie Yumin; on December 26, 2014, Dafei-related entities had repaid RMB 230 million to Xie Yumin through Dafei Real Estate Company; the parties unanimously confirmed that, as of February 6, 2015, the remaining debt owed by Party C and Party D to Xie Yumin was RMB 325.1 million; regarding the transfer of Party A's claims against Dafei to Party B, the parties had made arrangements between themselves. According to that arrangement, Party A now agreed to retain RMB 20 million of the right to receive payment from Party B, and the remaining portion would be transferred to Party E as agreed.

On September 5, 2015, Aoxinlong Company and Xie Yumin issued a Letter of Undertaking to Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company. Under the condition that Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company satisfied the seven conditions listed in the Letter of Undertaking, Aoxinlong Company and Xie Yumin undertook: 1. To cooperate with Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company in issuing documents such as a payment settlement letter and a letter of undertaking to apply to Cinda for payment of the RMB 200 million transaction price for Dali Huayuan, of which RMB 100 million would be paid to Dafei for its operational funding needs, and RMB 100 million would be used as repayment of Xie Yumin's historical debt; 2. To agree to extend the period for Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company to redeem the 99% equity of Meidafei Company to March 21, 2016. If Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company satisfied the seven conditions and redeemed the 99% equity of Meidafei Company before March 21, 2016, the redemption price as of that date would be RMB 1.257 billion. Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company signed and sealed the Letter of Undertaking, indicating their agreement and confirmation of its contents.

Zhang Yufang did not submit evidence to prove that he had, in accordance with the time limits and conditions stipulated in the Share Repurchase Agreement and the Letter of Undertaking, tendered the purchase to Aoxinlong Company for the redemption of the Meidafei Company's equity in question.

On October 23, 2015, Chuangdongfang Enterprise as the transferor and Aoxinlong Company as the transferee jointly signed an Equity Transfer Agreement, agreeing on the transfer of 99% equity of Meidafei Company by the transferor to the transferee for RMB 682,555,000, and stipulating that after the agreement took effect, the parties would handle the registration of change with the Market Supervision Bureau of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province in accordance with the law. On the same day, Shenzhen United Property Rights Exchange issued a Certificate of Witness for Equity Transfer for the Equity Transfer Agreement.

According to the information registered with the Market Supervision Administration of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province, on October 27, 2015, the legal representative of Meidafei Company changed from Yang Weiru to Xie Yumin; the term of operation changed from December 26, 1995 to December 26, 2015, to December 26, 2025; the equity composition changed from Chuangdongfang Enterprise holding 100% equity to Dafei Company holding 1% equity and Aoxinlong Company holding 99% equity; the directors changed from Yang Weiru (Chairman), Xiao Shuilong, Zhang Yufang, Chen Jing, and Guan Bin to Xie Yumin (Chairman), Huang Boya, and Tang Chunming; the supervisor changed from Wang Zhimin to Feng Jianning; the general manager changed from Yang Weiru to Xie Yumin.

On December 6, 2016, Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company as Party A, Aoxinlong Company as Party B, Xie Yumin as Party C, Zhang Baochen, Zhang Yan, and Yufang Company as Party D signed a Settlement Agreement, reaching a settlement regarding the performance of the Share Repurchase Agreement and the Letter of Undertaking, with a total settlement amount of RMB 2.268 billion. This settlement amount was to be resolved in a lump sum through the following two methods: The first method was that Hong Kong Meida International Business Company would transfer its 10% equity in Dafei Real Estate Company to Xie Yumin or his designee at a price of RMB 1, and its value would be assessed based on market fair value or agreed price, ultimately offsetting the above RMB 2.268 billion settlement amount at the confirmed price; the second method was that the parties would seek financing from Cinda Company through the Meidafei Company's Fuyong project, and the financing obtained would be used to pay the balance of the settlement amount after the calculation under the first method. The Settlement Agreement also stipulated that the purpose of signing this agreement was only for settlement between the parties and not for any purpose detrimental to the parties; it would be invalid if used for other purposes. The parties have not submitted evidence to prove that this Settlement Agreement has been fully performed.

(4) Status of the land in question under Meidafei Company

According to the Notice of Disposal Plan for Idle Land issued by the Bao'an Administration Bureau of the Shenzhen Municipal Planning and Land Resources Commission to Meidafei Company on November 16, 2015, it was stated that the four parcels of land owned by Meidafei Company located in Fuyong Street, Bao'an District, Shenzhen, covering an area of approximately 335,708 square meters, were designated for the construction of an industrial zone, comprehensive buildings, and living supporting facilities. These lands were acquired by Meidafei Company through a court auction in 1996. The four parcels of land were determined to be idle land. The disposal plan approved by the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government was: "For land that has been approved for conversion to commercial/residential, complete the procedures and continue development; for green space and roads, purchase back with compensation; for the remainder, if there are projects, verify the land scale, complete procedures, and continue development; otherwise, take back." On April 13, 2020, the Bao'an Administration Bureau of the Shenzhen Municipal Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources issued a Reply on Matters Concerning the Fuyong Land of Shenzhen Meidafei Investment Development Co., Ltd. to Meidafei Company, stating: Given that the Fuyong land had been included in the city's special action for disposal of approved but undeconstructed land, it was recommended to wait for the district government's clear disposal opinion before handling subsequent procedures according to regulations. The land in question is still held by Meidafei Company.

(5) Handling of Case No. 1 of the Guangdong High Court

In January 2017, Dafei Company filed a first-instance lawsuit with that court as the plaintiff, naming Aoxinlong Company, Xie Yumin, Chen Jing, and Guangdian Company as defendants, and Medaifei Company as the third party, requesting confirmation that the legal relationship between Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company and Xie Yumin was a loan relationship, and that after repayment, 55.14% of the 99% equity in Medaifei Company held by Aoxinlong Company should belong to Dafei Company. After trial, that court held that, according to the relevant provisions of the Equity Repurchase Agreement, during the repurchase period stipulated in the agreement and the extension period agreed to by Aoxinlong Company, the disputed equity held by Aoxinlong Company exhibited certain characteristics of investment guarantee measures, but after the expiration of the repurchase period, Aoxinlong Company had genuinely held the disputed equity. That court therefore rendered a judgment on July 6, 2021, dismissing all of Dafei Company's claims. Dafei Company appealed, and the case is currently under second-instance trial in this court.

Opinion of the Court: Zhang Yufang is a national of Belize. Pursuant to Article 1(1) of the Interpretation (I) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations and Article 3 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Establishment of the International Commercial Court, this case is an international commercial case. At the trial, Zhang Yufang, Xie Yumin, Aoxinlong Company, Liu Hechao, and Chen Jing all agreed that the laws of the People's Republic of China should apply to the hearing of this case. According to Article 3 of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations, which provides that the parties may expressly choose the law applicable to foreign-related civil relations in accordance with the provisions of the law, the laws of the People's Republic of China shall apply as the governing law to this case.

Based on Zhang Yufang's claims and in light of the defenses submitted by Xie Yumin, Aoxinlong Company, Liu Hechao, and Chen Jing, the issues in dispute in this case are: 1. whether this case constitutes a repetitive lawsuit with Guangdong High Court Case No. 1; 2. whether the plaintiff has standing to bring this action and whether Liu Hechao and Chen Jing may be named as defendants in this case; 3. whether the transaction involving 99% of the equity of Medaifei Company in this case constitutes a private lending and security by transfer or a dispute over equity transfer and repurchase contract, and if it constitutes a security by transfer, whether it should be confirmed that the 43.86% equity of Medaifei Company held by Aoxinlong Company belongs to the plaintiff; and 4. whether the four defendants should be jointly and severally liable to the plaintiff for compensation of RMB 500,000 in losses.

1. Whether this case constitutes a repetitive lawsuit.

Article 247(1) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides: "Where a party initiates another action on a matter that has already been filed in court during the proceedings or after a judgment has taken effect, and the following conditions are all met, it constitutes a repetitive action: (1) the parties in the subsequent action and the prior action are the same; (2) the subject matter of the subsequent action and the prior action is the same; (3) the claims in the subsequent action and the prior action are the same, or the claims in the subsequent action essentially negate the judgment result of the prior action." In this case, the plaintiff is Zhang Yufang, while the plaintiff in Guangdong High Court Case No. 1 is Dafei Company. The main claim of Zhang Yufang in this case is to confirm that the 43.86% equity of Medaifei Company registered under the name of Aoxinlong Company belongs to him, while the main claim in Case No. 1 is to confirm that the 55.14% equity of Medaifei Company under the name of Aoxinlong Company belongs to Dafei Company. Therefore, the parties and claims in the two cases differ, and they cannot substitute for or encompass each other. Hence, this case and Case No. 1 do not constitute a repetitive lawsuit. The defenses of Xie Yumin and Aoxinlong Company that this case and Case No. 1 constitute a repetitive lawsuit cannot be sustained.

2. Whether the plaintiff has standing to bring this action and whether Liu Hechao and Chen Jing may be named as defendants.

According to Article 122 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, apart from other conditions, an action must meet the following condition: the plaintiff is a citizen, legal person, or other organization that has a direct interest in the case. In this case, the plaintiff, Zhang Yufang, is a signatory to the Equity Repurchase Agreement involved in the case and, under the agreement, often bore relevant rights and obligations together with Dafei Company as a whole. Now, claiming in his own name based on the contract involved that his civil rights and interests have been infringed or that he has a civil dispute with the defendants, he should be deemed to have standing as a plaintiff. Therefore, the defense of Xie Yumin and Aoxinlong Company that Zhang Yufang lacks standing is not supported by this court. Article 122 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that when initiating an action, the plaintiff must have a definite defendant. Liu Hechao is a party to the Principle Framework Agreement dated December 18, 2014, which is closely related to the Equity Repurchase Agreement in this case, and Chen Jing is a party to the Medaifei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement dated September 26, 2013, and both are also parties to other contracts involved in this case. Therefore, they may be named as defendants. Accordingly, the claims of Liu Hechao that he is not a party to the contract and of Chen Jing that he is not a proper defendant are not supported by this court. As to the issues of the factual and legal basis for the plaintiff's request that the defendants bear liability and whether the defendants should bear corresponding civil liability, the people's court shall make a substantive judgment after comprehensive consideration based on the facts found and the applicable law.

3. Whether the nature of the change in the 99% equity of Medaifei Company in this case and whether the 43.86% equity therein should belong to Zhang Yufang.

Prior to the Equity Repurchase Agreement involved in this case, the parties in this case and relevant persons not involved in the case had signed the Cooperation Agreement and a series of supplementary agreements, the Medaifei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement, and the Supplementary Agreement (II) to the Medaifei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement. After the Equity Repurchase Agreement, there were also the Letter of Undertaking and the Settlement Agreement. This case mainly concerns the performance of the Equity Repurchase Agreement and does not involve the performance of the prior related agreements and supplementary agreements. The Equity Repurchase Agreement involved in this case was entered into by numerous parties and its terms are complex. In terms of content, the subject matter of the contract includes equity of Medaifei Company, historical debts of RMB 548.96 million, equity of Aoxinlong Company, proceeds from Xinda Company, repurchase of equity of Medaifei Company from Chuangdongfang Enterprise, equity of Dafei Company, etc., encompassing several legal relationships, making it a composite, atypical commercial contract.

Although the Equity Repurchase Agreement involved in this case arranged several commercial transactions, the focus of the dispute in this case mainly concerns the nature of the equity change under the said agreement. Regarding this, Zhang Yufang contends that the Equity Repurchase Agreement is in substance a private lending contract in the name of an equity repurchase agreement, that the transfer of 43.86% of the equity of Medaifei Company to be registered under the name of Aoxinlong Company was a security by transfer of equity to secure the realization of the creditor's right, and that the equity of Medaifei Company involved in this case still belongs to Zhang Yufang. Aoxinlong Company and Xie Yumin argue that the Equity Repurchase Agreement is a contract for equity transfer, that Xie Yumin has invested RMB 682.555 million to acquire 99% of the equity of Medaifei Company, and that Aoxinlong Company's acceptance of the assignment of the equity of Medaifei Company was based on a genuine equity transfer with a repurchase clause, not a security by transfer. This court holds that the distinction between security by transfer and equity transfer should mainly be judged based on the purpose of the contract and whether the contract has the characteristic of principal and accessory relationships. Article 71 of the Minutes of the National Conference on Civil and Commercial Trial Work provides: "If a debtor or a third party enters into a contract with a creditor, agreeing to formally transfer property to the name of the creditor, and the debtor repays the debt when due, whereupon the creditor returns the property to the debtor or the third party, and if the debtor fails to repay the debt when due, the creditor may auction, sell, or discount the property to satisfy the claim, this constitutes a security by transfer, and the people's court shall find the contract valid." It can be seen from this that security by transfer, as an atypical security, aims to provide security for the principal debt and belongs to the category of accessory contracts; regarding the transferred property, the transferee may not exercise relevant rights or dispose of the security property before the principal debt falls due. Property right transfer or equity transfer, as a transaction arrangement, aims to obtain the consideration payable by the buyer after transferring the property right or equity, and is a contractual act in which the seller delivers the transferred property in exchange for the consideration in accordance with the contract terms. This can be specifically divided into the following three points:

First, the terms of the contract contain no content regarding security by transfer and do not reflect the principal-accessory nature of the contract. In terms of the content of the agreement, according to the recital clauses and the provisions of Articles 1 and 2 of the agreement, Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company originally owed Xie Yumin historical debts of RMB 548.96 million; the 90% equity of Aoxinlong Company originally registered under Xie Yumin's name and the 10% equity of Aoxinlong Company registered under Guangdian Company's name were held by way of security by transfer; the equity of Medaifei Company was originally held 56.14% by Dafei Company and 43.86% by Aoxinlong Company, but due to borrowing from Chuangdongfang Enterprise to repay debts, 100% of Medaifei Company was transferred and registered under the name of Chuangdongfang Enterprise; since Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company agreed that Xie Yumin would assist Aoxinlong Company in raising funds to repurchase from Chuangdongfang Enterprise 100% of the equity of Medaifei Company, Xie Yumin's holding of 90% of the equity of Aoxinlong Company was no longer a guarantee method for the aforementioned historical debts, but was formally held by Xie Yumin; because when Chuangdongfang Enterprise released the equity of Medaifei Company, 99% of the equity was held by Aoxinlong Company and 1% by Dafei Company, according to Article 1 of the Equity Repurchase Agreement regarding Xie Yumin formally holding equity of Aoxinlong Company, Xie Yumin should also indirectly hold equity of Medaifei Company through formal holding of equity of Aoxinlong Company. From the above, it can be seen that the content of the Equity Repurchase Agreement does not contain provisions on lending between Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company to Xie Yumin, nor does it arrange for the 99% equity of Medaifei Company to be transferred to Xie Yumin and Aoxinlong Company as security by transfer, and there is no clause reflecting the principal-accessory nature of the contract. Therefore, Zhang Yufang's contention that the 99% equity of Medaifei Company registered under the name of Aoxinlong Company was a security by transfer of equity provided by Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company to Xie Yumin lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported by this court. At the same time, Zhang Yufang's assertion that the value of the disputed equity is the basis for determining whether the legal relationship regarding the equity change in the Equity Repurchase Agreement is a loan guarantee relationship or an equity transfer relationship is also not supported by this court, as the decisive factor in distinguishing between equity transfer and security by transfer is not the value of the equity as he claims.

Second, the Equity Repurchase Agreement involved in this case arranged for the equity repurchase. Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company had previously participated in signing the Cooperation Agreement, the Medaifei Fuyong Project Cooperation Agreement, and Supplementary Agreement II, where terms such as "holding on behalf" and "risk safeguard measures" were used when describing the method of holding equity, whereas in signing the Equity Repurchase Agreement, Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company used terms such as "formally" and "actually" holding, reflecting a significant change in the intent of Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company in the complex commercial transaction involved in this case. To achieve their respective commercial purposes, the parties also set out the purchase right for the equity of Medaifei Company. Article 5 of the Equity Repurchase Agreement provides that Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company have the right to purchase from Aoxinlong Company the 99% equity of Medaifei Company within 12 months after Aoxinlong Company repurchases the equity of Medaifei Company from Chuangdongfang Enterprise on this occasion; and stipulates that if the equity is purchased within 6 months, the consideration is RMB 1.03 billion; if purchased within 6 to 12 months, the consideration is RMB 1.1 billion. It also provides for the treatment of the balance and difference after Aoxinlong Company realizes the investment proceeds by disposing of the equity of Medaifei Company: if the disposal amount exceeds the amount due to Aoxinlong Company (historical debts plus the agreed total repurchase price), the excess shall be enjoyed by Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company; if the disposal amount is insufficient to satisfy the amount due to Aoxinlong Company, the shortfall shall be borne by Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company. This court holds that the amount of the Medaifei project involved in this case is huge, the content of the relevant contracts or agreements is complex, and the arrangements between the parties are very specific and detailed, reflecting that the participating entities are all mature commercial transaction participants. The rights and obligations in commercial transactions are primarily determined by the parties' freely expressed intentions, and the law does not prohibit the conversion between debt investments and equity investments under certain conditions. Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company, as independent and mature commercial entities, had previously arranged for security by transfer in the process of holding equity in Medaifei Company, and should have known the difference between a security by transfer contract and an equity transfer contract. The agreement between the parties in this case regarding the equity transfer and the equity purchase right, i.e., the arrangement to protect their own interests by retaining the right to repurchase that portion of equity within a certain period after the equity transfer, without arranging for a security by transfer, i.e., without stipulating that Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company would repay the funds raised by Xie Yumin and Aoxinlong Company and obtain the equity of Medaifei Company, should be regarded as the most prudent consideration and arrangement of their own interests in light of the circumstances of the commercial transaction at that time. Since this commercial transaction agreement represents the true intention of the parties and was reached by consensus, and does not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, the agreement of the commercial entities should be respected, and each party should perform its obligations and bear civil liability in accordance with the agreement.

Third, after the expiration of the repurchase period, Aoxinlong Company formally held the equity of Medaifei Company and enjoyed full shareholder rights. Upon investigation, after the signing of the Equity Repurchase Agreement, Aoxinlong Company raised funds as agreed and paid Chuangdongfang Enterprise, which, upon receipt of payment, released 100% of the equity of Medaifei Company, and the equity structure of Medaifei Company changed to Aoxinlong Company holding 99% and Dafei Company holding 1%. At the same time, the legal representative and general manager of Medaifei Company were changed to Xie Yumin, and the supervisors and directors were also changed. According to Articles 2 and 6 of the Equity Repurchase Agreement, during the one-year repurchase period and the extension period agreed to by Aoxinlong Company (hereinafter collectively referred to as the repurchase period), Aoxinlong Company guaranteed that Medaifei Company would not engage in other unrelated operational work, that matters concerning external cooperation of Medaifei Company would be determined by Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company through consultation, that the relevant seals of Aoxinlong Company and Medaifei Company would be jointly managed by Dafei Company and Aoxinlong Company, and that they would not sell the equity and assets of Medaifei Company to third parties. From the above, it can be seen that during the repurchase period, Aoxinlong Company, as a shareholder of Medaifei Company, could not sell the equity of Medaifei Company externally, and its management rights were also subject to certain restrictions. Moreover, according to Article 5(5) of the Equity Repurchase Agreement, during the repurchase period, Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company retained control over the disputed equity and actually bore the risk of changes in the value of the disputed equity. However, after the expiration of the repurchase period, Aoxinlong Company could exercise management rights over the portion of equity of Medaifei Company it held, and there was no explicit restriction on the power of disposition. Subsequently, between Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company on one side and Xie Yumin and Aoxinlong Company on the other, the Letter of Undertaking and the Settlement Agreement were formed concerning the repurchase (or redemption) of the equity of Medaifei Company after the expiration of the one-year repurchase period, which on one hand reflected that after the overall value of the Medaifei project increased, the price for repurchasing the equity before March 21, 2016, was RMB 1.257 billion, and the total settlement amount on December 6, 2016, was RMB 2.268 billion. On the other hand, this arrangement further indicates that the equity change involved in this case was a arrangement for repurchase after transfer rather than a security by transfer. Now, because Zhang Yufang and Dafei Company failed to submit evidence proving that they had exercised the repurchase right on time and notified Xie Yumin and Aoxinlong Company, it should be determined that Aoxinlong Company has actually held the disputed equity in this case and enjoys full shareholder rights.

In addition, although Zhang Yufang was the original actual controller of Medaifei Company, the equity of Medaifei Company was originally held by two shareholders, Aoxinlong Company and Dafei Company, and he did not provide evidence that he had directly held equity in Medaifei Company. Moreover, even if Zhang Yufang had been the actual controller of Aoxinlong Company, Aoxinlong Company has an independent legal personality in the sense of company law, and Zhang Yufang has no reason to bypass Aoxinlong Company and directly claim equity in Medaifei Company. Therefore, Aoxinlong Company's argument that Zhang Yufang never held equity in Medaifei Company and lacks the basis for a claim to the equity involved is well-founded.

In summary, Zhang Yufang's contention that the 99% equity of Medaifei Company held by Aoxinlong Company constitutes a security by transfer, of which 43.86% should belong to him, lacks factual and legal basis, and Zhang Yufang also did not provide evidence that he had repaid the RMB 682.555 million. Therefore, this court does not support this claim.

4. Whether the four defendants should be jointly and severally liable for compensating the plaintiff for losses of RMB 500,000.

Zhang Yufang claims that during the repurchase period stipulated in the contract involved, relying on the repurchase commitments of Aoxinlong Company and Xie Yumin, he reached a financing cooperation intention with Xinda Company and paid a deposit of RMB 500,000, but due to the defendants' malicious obstruction, he suffered a loss of RMB 500,000, and requests that the four defendants be jointly and severally liable for compensation. Zhang Yufang submitted the reply letter from Xinda Company and relevant adjudicative documents and materials in an attempt to prove that the four defendants refused to cooperate with due diligence and maliciously obstructed his financing. Xie Yumin submitted evidence that Medaifei Company, Aoxinlong Company, and he himself had actively cooperated in the use of seals. This court holds that the evidence submitted by Zhang Yufang is insufficient to support his claim, and the parties subsequently signed the Settlement Agreement regarding the repurchase, which also was not performed. Therefore, Zhang Yufang's claim for joint and several compensation of RMB 500,000 by the four defendants lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported.

In summary, pursuant to Article 3 of the Law of the PRC on Choice of Law for Foreign-Related Civil Relations and Article 8 of the Contract Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

All claims of Zhang Yufang (ZHANG YUFANG) are dismissed.

The case acceptance fee is RMB 2,625,230, to be borne by Zhang Yufang (ZHANG YUFANG).

This judgment is final.
